official.description_text:
Doctoral student in hormone sensing between biophysics and biotechnology
Apply for position
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Engineering Sciences
Project description
Third-cycle subject:
Applied Physics or Biotechnology
Hormones shape metabolism, fertility, mood and sleep, yet they are rarely measured, and then mostly by blood tests in a clinic. In the Hormones Project, funded by KTH InspireLab, we are developing an affordable optical system that measures six hormones in urine, at home, every day. As a doctoral student you will work at the border between biophysics and biotechnology: you will prepare and characterise urine samples, validate against established laboratory methods, and design and test the detection system.
The project is jointly led by three research leaders at AlbaNova and SciLifeLab. Read more about the project
here
Supervision:
Carlota Canalias, Michael Fokine and Cecilia Williams are proposed to supervise the doctoral student. Decisions are made on admission.
Admission requirements
To be admitted to postgraduate education (Chapter 7, 39 § Swedish Higher Education Ordinance), the applicant must have basic eligibility in accordance with either of the following:
passed a second cycle degree (for example a master's degree), or
completed course requirements of at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 second-cycle higher education credits, or
acquired, in some other way within or outside the country, substantially equivalent knowledge
The candidate must have a master's degree in biophysics, biotechnology, biomedicine, physics or a closely related field.
In addition to the above, there is also a
mandatory requirement for English equivalent to English B/6.
Selection
In order to succeed as a doctoral student at KTH you need to be goal oriented and persevering in your work. During the selection process, candidates will be assessed upon their ability to:
independently pursue his or her work
collaborate with others,
have a professional approach,
analyze and work with complex issues,
demonstrate knowledge of gender equality from an intersectional perspective and an understanding of why gender aspects are important when conducting research and developing technology,
demonstrate good written and spoken English, as it is required in day to day work.
experience of laboratory work with optical, spectroscopic, biophysical or bioanalytical methods is considered a merit.
Experience of working in multidisciplinary teams is also a merit.
Furthermore, the candidate should have a genuine interest in learning new disciplines.
After the qualification requirements, great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Target degree: Doctoral degree
Information regarding admission and employment
Only those admitted to postgraduate education may be employed as a doctoral student. The total length of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education in four years' time. An employed doctoral student can, to a limited extent (maximum 20%), perform certain tasks within their role, e.g. training and administration. A new position as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, and then the employment may be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time. In the case of studies that are to be completed with a licentiate degree, the total period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for two years.
As a doctoral student, you are entitled to a workplace with
many employee benefits
and monthly salary according to
KTH’s Doctoral student salary agreement
. Read more about
Doctoral studies (PhD) | KTH | Sweden
.

To apply for the position
Apply for the position and admission through KTH's recruitment system. It is the applicant’s responsibility to ensure that the application is complete in accordance with the instructions in the advertisement.
Applications must include:
Copies of diplomas and grades from previous university studies and certificates of fulfilled
language requirements (see above)
. Translations into English or Swedish if the original document is not issued in one of these languages. Copies of originals must be
certified
.
CV including your relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Application letter with a brief description of why you want to pursue research studies, about what your academic interests are and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. (Maximum 2 pages long)
Representative publications or technical reports. For longer documents, please provide a summary (abstract) and a web link to the full text.
A statement (maximum 1 page) on your view of and vision for gender equality and technology.
A copy of your master's thesis or similar.
Applications must be received at the last closing date at midnight, CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).

ai.summary: Doctoral position (3–4 years) in biophysics/biotechnology developing an optical system for at-home hormone sensing using urine samples. Jointly supervised by researchers at KTH AlbaNova and SciLifeLab. Work spans sample preparation, validation, and optical detection system design.

thematic_fit.rationale: No thematic overlap. Position is rooted in optical biophysics, hormone biomarkers, and bioanalytical sensing. Researcher's expertise is human-centred immersive systems, spatial cognition, and collaborative learning. Neither biomedical sensing, optical physics, nor hormone analysis relate to immersive systems, wayfinding, or spatial learning research.

methodological_fit.rationale: Negligible methodological bridge. Position emphasises laboratory work (optical/spectroscopic/biophysical methods), sample characterisation, and instrumentation validation. Researcher's methodological strengths are user studies, experimental design (in learning/spatial contexts), and immersive system evaluation. Experimental design concept is shared, but application context (bioanalytical lab work vs. user evaluation in spatial/immersive settings) is entirely distinct. No transferable methodological value.

growth_value.rationale: Essentially zero growth value for stated target identity. Doctoral work in optical biophysics and hormone sensing closes no gaps relevant to human-centred immersive systems, spatial learning, or collaborative interaction research. Would require complete disciplinary reorientation and offer no pathway back to target identity.

strategic_value.rationale: Limited strategic value. KTH is a strong technical university in Sweden (preferred country per constraints), which is positive for geographic fit. However, doctoral studies in biomedical sensing do not advance researcher's target trajectory. Supervisors are biophysicists/biotechnologists with no evident HCI or immersive systems background. PhD completion would confer advanced research credentials, but in a domain entirely orthogonal to human-centred XR/HCI. Unlikely to strengthen candidacy for postdoctoral or research roles in target field.

eligibility_flags: Position requires master's degree in biophysics, biotechnology, biomedicine, physics, or closely related field. Researcher holds MSc by Research in multimedia/creative multimedia (in progress). Multimedia is not listed as closely related. Institutional eligibility unclear without explicit exemption or reinterpretation of 'closely related'.
Mandatory English requirement (B/6 level or higher); researcher meets this (fluent English demonstrated).
Security clearance mentioned as possible requirement (Protective Security Act). Researcher's profile does not indicate security-sensitive background; risk/barrier level unclear.
Emphasis on laboratory work with optical, spectroscopic, biophysical, or bioanalytical methods as merit. Researcher has no documented experience in these areas.
risks: Disciplinary barrier: multimedia/XR is not an accepted pathway to biophysics/biotechnology doctoral studies. Strong likelihood of desk-reject or admission refusal based on educational background.
No domain expertise: researcher has no coursework, publications, or experience in biophysics, biotechnology, or biomedical sensing. Starting from scratch in a 3–4 year programme is high-risk.

Complete direction divergence: doctoral work would move researcher into biomedical instrumentation, away from human-centred systems research. Three-year investment yields no advancement toward target identity (human-centred immersive systems, spatial learning, collaboration).

Career continuity risk: post-doctoral positioning would be confusing to HCI/XR research communities. Unlikely to be competitive for postdoctoral or research roles in target field after biomedical sensing doctorate.
